A p CASL perfusion fMRI sequence was used for resting baseline, SC and non-SC data acquisition.
Imaging was conducted on a Siemens Trio 3T whole body scanner (Erlangen, Germany) using an 8-channel head coil.

Interleaved images with and without labeling were obtained using a gradient echo echo-planar sequence with a delay of 1.5 or 1 ms inserted between the end of the labeling pulse and image acquisition (FOV = 220 mm, matrix = 64 × 64 × 18, TR = 4000 ms, TE = 17 ms, flip angle = 90°, slice thickness = 6 mm with a 7.2 mm gap).

Interleaved images with and without labeling were obtained using a gradient echo echo-planar sequence with a delay of 1.5 or 1 ms inserted between the end of the labeling pulse and image acquisition (FOV = 220 mm, matrix = 64 × 64 × 18, TR = 4000 ms, TE = 17 ms, flip angle = 90°, slice thickness = 6 mm with a 7.2 mm gap).

For both SC and non-SC scans, 68 CBF image series were generated from the 136 label/control ASL image pairs using a simplified two-compartment model with the sinc interpolation method for CBF calculations ( ).

During each session, participants completed brain scans in the following order: a high resolution structural scan, a 5 min resting perfusion baseline scan, a 5 min BOLD resting baseline scan, a 9 min non-SC p CASL scan, and a 9 min SC p CASL scan.

For task-related fMRI, data was collected using a gradient echo-planar sequence with the following parameters: TR = 2 s, TE = 30 ms, clip angle = 75°, slices = 37, distance factor 10%, voxel size = 3.5 mm isotropic and a GRAPPA acceleration factor of 2.
